title: Scope reduction: Activity Stream + Cost Heatmap MVP; defer Trace Flamegraphs & Route Histograms
creator: Ava Chen
description: Context: We need a compact observability surface for Console that delivers high-value signals to customers while keeping implementation and infra cost within the 2026 Q1 budget. The original scope included multiple route-level histograms, flamegraphs, and session-level trace replay. After cross-functional review we are cutting scope to ship two high-leverage tiles: (1) Activity Stream — a chronological, filterable list of bucketed events for the selected workspace/time-range; (2) Cost Heatmap — a 2D heatmap showing cost density by time-of-day vs route group, with quick top-N route cost breakdown. Deferred: per-request flamegraphs, full route-level latency histograms, and session replay.
acceptance_criteria: Activity Stream tile loads within 400ms on initial render for a workspace with <= 10M tokens/day and paginates with cursor-based 200-item batches
Activity Stream supports filters: time range, route tag, model family, and severity; combined filters return results within 250ms for typical queries
Each Activity Stream item includes timestamp, route id, model variant, token count, request cost estimate, and a link to the raw request/response in logs (s3/gcs link or internal tracing view)
Cost Heatmap shows aggregated cost density per route-group x hour-of-day for the selected 7/30/90 day windows and renders within 600ms for typical workspace sizes

Cost Heatmap provides an interactive top-10 routes panel that lists cumulative cost, calls, average latency, and a 'drill to traces' link that opens the tracing workspace (link only; detailed flamegraphs deferred)
All telemetry queries use existing aggregated billing indexes; no new per-request retention tiers are required for MVP
Console UI gracefully degrades: if aggregated cost indexes are stale or missing, show informative empty state with CTA to run manual backfill
End-to-end QA pass: smoke tests, filter edge cases, accessibility checks (keyboard nav + screen reader label coverage), and load test for parallel 50 concurrent users without >5% error rate
decisions: Ship Activity Stream + Cost Heatmap as the minimum viable observability surface to provide both operational signal (Activity Stream) and economic signal (Cost Heatmap)
Defer per-request flamegraphs and full route histograms to a follow-up epic to reduce front-end complexity and backend retention costs
Prefer link-outs to existing tracing systems rather than embedding trace UI for MVP to avoid adding new instrumented UI code paths
Use existing aggregated billing index (billing-agg-v2) as the data source; if missing, surface a backfill CTA instead of blocking the surface
tradeoffs: Pro: Faster ship, lower infra cost; Con: Reduced forensic capability out of the box — operators must click-through to tracing for deep dives
Pro: Simpler front-end code with two modular tiles; Con: Less completion of analysts' workflow within a single page (extra context switching)
Risk: Some customers expect per-route latency histograms — communicate clearly in UI and docs that these are deferred and link to tracing
implementation_notes: Frontend: implement two new React tile components with lazy load; reuse existing charting primitives from telemetry library
Backend: add two thin GraphQL endpoints that proxy to billing-agg-v2 and activity-agg indices; enforce 5s timeout and 10k-result cap
Auth: reuse RBAC checks from console-viz — tiles hidden if workspace lacks billing read permissions
Observability: instrument queries with trace id and expose token-level cost breakdown for debugging; add a runtime feature flag (console.activity.costheatmap.v1) for gradual rollout
Data: confirm billing-agg-v2 supports the group-by needed; if not, implement a scheduled pre-aggregation job (low-priority) — this must not block MVP launch
followups: EPIC PM-100412: Implement route-level histograms & flamegraph embedding (target Q2)
ENG-22345: Preaggregation job for rare workspaces with >100M tokens/day (opt-in backfill)
DES-11987: Refine Activity Stream accessibility and compact density layout based on first-week usage data
PM-980322: Post-launch validation: 2-week telemetry review + customer feedback sync to decide next slices
qa_checks: Keyboard navigation across both tiles with focus outlines and aria-labels verified
Simulate empty and partial-aggregation states and validate empty-state CTAs
Run load test scenario 'observability-mvp-50u' and collect P95 latency and error metrics
Validate links to tracing open correct workspace and preserve time-range and route context
rollout_plan: Enable behind feature flag; internal dogfood for 48 hours
Phased 10% -> 50% -> 100% rollout over 5 days, monitor error budget and query latencies
If query latency > 1.5x baseline or errors > 3%, roll back to previous flag state and open incident
Collect qualitative feedback via customer success for first five enterprise accounts that opt into alpha
